patches.title: Split fused tool-call arguments into separate calls
patches.symptom: Tool call "<name>": Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position N — Received arguments:\n{...}{...}
patches.rootCause: The relay can stream two tool calls into one index. @earendil-works/pi-ai parseToolCallArguments (dist/utils/json-parse.js) receives the concatenation, throws LlmError(MALFORMED_RESPONSE), and @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop re-throws because MALFORMED_RESPONSE is not in the default retryableCodes. Measured at dsh-llm-pi-ai/lib/index.js:1656 and confirmed upstream in deepseek-harness discussion #4427.
limits: cannot recover a call whose tail was cut by max-tokens (finish.reason.kind === length)
does not fix the relay or adapter that assigned one index to two calls
does not reorder or rename calls; the first call keeps the original id
cannot attribute which upstream stage glued the objects; it only sees the assembled text

patches.title: A rescue must be provable, attributable and atomic
patches.symptom: a split-out call could run under an empty or wrong tool name, a repaired finish could replay without replayState, and a block-end repair could be committed before a later block of the same stream was rejected
patches.rootCause: repair-stream committed each block-end repair as it arrived, kept only the last name seen on an index, and emitted {kind:"stop"} without the adapter replayState; none of that broke the JSON proof, so a repaired call could still be dispatched wrong
limits: on rc.1 the adapter never closed a tool-call block; on rc.3 it closes the first fragment and leaves the surplus to the finish path
a synthesized block-start is proven on the finish path only (BS-11)
a fusion of two different tools carries one name per index; the surplus goes out under remedy_unattributed (BS-18)
a tool name that arrives twice with different values stays unrepairable

patches.title: A refusal must be observable, and a withdrawal must not read as a repair
patches.symptom: a stream whose only defect is plain bad JSON read "repair incomplete", and a withdrawn repair was indistinguishable from a fusion nobody could split
patches.rootCause: recordRejected incremented fused and unrepaired for every rejection whatever its code, so a refusal that never proved a fusion inflated fused — the difference between "we declined" and "we could not" was erased
limits: the four verdict states and their order are unchanged: the counts are reported, never judged
no state name can say "observed, refused, and correctly not repaired"; only the counter row carries it
old journal lines keep the six-field shape: no migration rewrites them

patches.title: A bare value after a member key must be resealed, or refused — never guessed
patches.symptom: a tool call fails with `Unexpected token` or `Unexpected end of JSON input` because the model wrote a program, not a JSON string, after `"code":`; the turn dies and nothing is repaired
patches.rootCause: a bare unquoted multi-line blob as one member value is neither a fusion nor splittable, so P-0001 refused it as `single-object` and the call never dispatched
limits: reseals only when exactly one member value proves; two possible resealings is refused as ambiguous
never touches a truncated call; a duplicate key, doubled colon, missing brace or illegal escape stays a refusal
keeps the call id: no synthetic identity, and the stream budget is untouched

patches.title: A second seam with no test is a seam nobody has ever run
patches.symptom: agent/request-error shipped in 0.2.0 behind retryOnMalformed with zero tests; it called next() and then overrode the answer, kept its budget in a Map that was never pruned, and would have retried IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED / INVALID_CREDENTIAL / MISSING_CREDENTIAL
patches.rootCause: the listener was written against an assumed contract. The shipped runtime says a handling listener returns {kind:"retry"} without calling next(), and a waterfall listener that does not own the decision must return next(); calling next() first discards the default chain, and context compaction authorizes its own retry on that path
limits: only MALFORMED_RESPONSE is retried; SERVER, TRANSPORT and TIMEOUT already self-heal upstream (195 of 213 failing groups), so a second layer would compete for the seam
the retry budget defaults to 0: nothing is retried unless a deployment asks for it
the bound is 256 cache entries; an evicted entry lets a very long single turn spend a fresh retry
no live artifact: the headless profile never failed in a way this plugin retries at the default budget

patches.title: One byte cap for two load paths is a cap that taxes the wrong half
patches.symptom: the single 68000-byte ceiling counted a mounted plugin and a CLI invocation as the same thing. P-0009 landed with three bytes of headroom, and the next patch (P-0011) needed 4263 bytes of new module that simply did not fit: the only way to pay for it under the old cap was to delete prose from files a daemon loads at startup
patches.rootCause: scripts/gate_size.mjs summed every emitted module and compared one number. It never asked which of those modules a running plugin imports, so 31425 bytes of CLI-only code (cli, cli-args, scan-command, session-scan) sat inside the same budget as the 38073 bytes that actually load on every session, and every resident byte had to be financed out of the CLI half
limits: it still refuses a crossing; the caps moved twice in one session (R20) and both moves are recorded in scripts/lib/budgets.mjs with the owner signature PROJECT_RULES section 1 requires
the class lists are explicit, but the governance test only checks the relative import graph: a module pulled in through dsh-remedy-core or a dynamic import would not be caught
a split budget cannot tell good growth from bad; it only says which half pays
it caps emitted JavaScript only, not declarations, fixtures or package-root files

patches.title: The failure class this host hits most after fusion was named by nobody
patches.symptom: 37 turns on this host died with UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT (one sentence, three workspaces, eleven sessions); scan counted them and the resident layer said nothing. INVALID_REQUEST, MISSING_CREDENTIAL and EMPTY_RESPONSE were silent in the same way
patches.rootCause: repair-stream is mounted on llm/stream, so a step refused during preparation never reaches it; the error code and its message existed and had no path into the journal
limits: naming is always on and never repairs or retries: one named line instead of one dead turn
preflight is a pure decision, not a mount; nothing wires it into agent/pre-step yet, because P-0015 measures that seam first
it never silently downgrades a level: the adapter would, the user decides, so the patch reports a suggestion instead
a model whose metadata lives only in the adapter is reported as unknown, never assumed

patches.title: A scan must read the log it is pointed at, and a redaction must see every path shape
patches.symptom: `dsh-remedy scan <session.v4.jsonl.zstd>` reported 0 attempts and one unreadable line per compressed byte, and artifacts that cited a session file carried the account name in three shapes the redactor could not match
patches.rootCause: cmdScan read a multi-frame zstd session with readFileSync(file, "utf8") instead of the decompressSessionLog reader the plugin already ships (packages/plugin/src/cli.ts:236 in 0.3.2), and core/redact.ts matched only a single-backslash C:\Users\<name>, so a JSON-escaped path, a slashed path and a DSH session directory named after the home path all passed through.
limits: reports a filtered scan as before_since instead of guessing; an unstamped event inside a window is unreadable, never assumed in the window
one undecompressable file is a failures line and exit 3, not a silent zero
does not deduplicate the same repair seen by both the journal and the session file
matches a home path only when the directory starts with a drive letter; another workspace spelling is unmeasured

patches.title: A scan that counts only the repairable turns is not a fault map
patches.symptom: `scan` reported 44 fusion failures of 287 finished turns; the 88 `max-tokens` and 36 `UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT` turns were counted nowhere
patches.rootCause: session-scan.ts returned early on `kind !== "error"` and on `code !== "MALFORMED_RESPONSE"`: a filter for "can this layer repair it" carried into a map of "how the turn ended"
limits: reported, never promoted: the exit code still turns on fused_calls and fusion_failures
truncated turns stay unfixed; fusion_failures keeps its exact MALFORMED_RESPONSE meaning
a reason.kind this census does not know is left uncounted, not bucketed

patches.title: A copy channel that reports "exited null" cannot be repaired
patches.symptom: the two longest outward files could not be regenerated at all: every attempt printed `agy exited null`, so two different faults had one unreadable name
patches.rootCause: the request (35509 chars for changelog, 33530 for readme) exceeded the 32767-character Windows command line, so spawnSync failed with ENAMETOOLONG and a null status; a spawn killed by the timeout reported the same null. Transport is now chosen by request length
limits: no retry across transports: it picks one from the request length and reports the failure
the timeout is raised to half an hour, not removed; a failure is diagnosed, never repaired
the fact pack is not shortened to fit: argv only serves the smallest briefs

patches.title: A byte budget that no script checks is a suggestion
patches.symptom: the byte budget was crossed three times in a row (55815 after P-0005, 64539 after P-0004, 70389 on the first P-0006 attempt) and every crossing was found by hand after the build
patches.rootCause: the caps lived only in the fact pack and README.md; nothing under scripts/ read them, so a patch that crossed a line stayed green through the whole suite. The number had no mechanism
limits: the gate measures the emitted plugin only: core does not load at startup, so the ceiling protects what is loaded there
it does not shrink anything; the measured numbers stay what they were when the gate was written
it does not measure dist/*.d.ts, which is paid at build time rather than load time
it cannot decide how to split a file that crosses a cap — it only refuses the crossing, so the structural fix stays a human decision

patches.title: The npm page documented a CLI that had not existed since 0.3.3
patches.symptom: packages/plugin/README.md (the page npm renders) said scan <session.jsonl> [--json] [--out <file>] and the CLI USAGE said scan <session.jsonl|session.v4.jsonl.zstd> [--json] [--out <file>]; neither admitted a directory, --since or --max-files, all shipped by P-0004
patches.rootCause: nothing watched either string: gate_copy covers the root outward files, the package README has no output_sha256 and no gate, and no test ran --help or compared the two strings, so a red result was impossible
limits: the gate set still does not cover packages/*/README.md: the test compares the two scan lines, not the package README as a whole
moving the page into the copy channel would make it generated, which is a separate decision
the one-line-per-command rewrite pays for the flag list, so the per-command prose is thinner; the detail lives in the patch document
a usage string is not a resident seam: no live artifact, so this stays tested

patches.title: A windowed scan called the one dated line every session starts with unreadable
patches.symptom: scan --since over a real session directory reported unreadable_lines equal to the number of files it read: 78 files produced 78 unreadable lines while every byte of them parsed. The tool answered "I could not read this" about the single most reliable event in the log
patches.rootCause: packages/plugin/src/session-scan.ts:178 required a numeric `time` before it would apply the window and counted anything else as unreadable. A session log opens with a `{"type":"session",…}` header whose instant is `createdAt`, not `time`, so every header fell into that branch. The scanner was reading the file correctly and reporting the schema wrong
limits: only the `session` header is dated by createdAt; an ordinary event with no instant is still an unreadable line, because there is no second field to fall back to
the fix does not make the scan faster or smaller — it changes which bucket a header lands in
a header inside the window contributes its instant to the reported window but adds no attempts or turns, so the census does not move
it does not validate createdAt against the wall clock of the file; a hand-edited session can still claim any date

patches.title: The project describing itself is the part nothing checked
patches.symptom: the fact pack pinned core 0.3.7 and called 0.3.6 the previous release while the published 0.3.8 tarball pinned 0.3.8 and README/CHANGELOG named 0.3.7; the handoff quoted 900820ae for a file that hashes to 96f9144f; and the npm page documented four commands after explain shipped
patches.rootCause: the copy criterion checked the shape of a claim (every prose number exists in the fact pack) and never the pack own statements; gate_ssot validates data/results/*.json and never a hash printed in prose; cli-usage.test.ts compared one line, exactly as far as P-0010 needed
limits: the package README is still hand-written prose; its equality with USAGE is the guard, not a hash against the fact pack, so the rest of the page stays unguarded (BS-13 narrows)
the fact pack is checked only against other repository files; a sentence nothing else records stays an unverified claim about the world
the hash check skips any evidence row that compares two publishes rather than guessing
gate_copy still cannot see the handoff or the package README: these are governance tests, not gates

patches.title: The seam nobody mounted because nobody measured what refusing looks like
patches.symptom: agent/pre-step stayed unmounted on one sentence repeated in three places: "a rejected step opens no step, but what the user sees has not been measured". A seam that can refuse before a token was blocked by an unchecked assumption
patches.rootCause: the claim was never run. The loop source answers it: preStep awaits the waterfall and, on {kind:"reject"}, closes the turn with reason "blocked" and no step
limits: it measures the seam, it does not mount a product on it: nothing calls agent/pre-step in a shipped profile
the desktop UI render of reason.kind "blocked" stays unmeasured, and the probe ran headless only
a rejection discards the claimed input: the user retypes the message, so {kind:"enter"} is the better default
only the first proposed step of one turn was exercised

patches.title: The command that answers "what covers this" kept its own copy of the answer
patches.symptom: `explain` answered "what covers this class" from its own COVERAGE and SWITCHES constants, so the registry and the command were two homes for one claim and nothing compared them
patches.rootCause: the command predates the registry carrying that claim; its local tables were the only map a user read, and a human diff by eye was the only mechanism
limits: moves six claims and no behaviour: the printed table is identical before and after
switch keys stay a closed vocabulary (repair, retryOnMalformed); another key must be added, not inferred
a covered-but-unmounted patch still reads covered-and-off: coverage is a claim about the code

patches.title: The two pages npm renders had no mechanism at all
patches.symptom: both package pages are hand-written with no output_sha256 and no copy-channel entry, so gate_copy never saw them; 2331 bytes of the plugin page was compared against nothing while being what a stranger installs from
patches.rootCause: the copy channel was built for the repository-root files, and the package pages predate it; each round pinned one more line instead of answering what else was unguarded
limits: proves no prose number and no undispatchable command can rot; layout and behavioural claims stay hand-written
the number rule is the copy channel criterion, not a truth test, so a page can still describe absent behaviour
core/README.md is held to the weaker half only: it documents a library, not a command

patches.title: A Windows exit code printed as a bare number sent an operator hunting the wrong cause
patches.symptom: the publish wrapper printed "npm exited 3221226505 in packages/core" and then HTTP-shaped advice, so the operator hunted a credentials problem; that number is Windows 0xC0000409, raised before npm spoke to the registry
patches.rootCause: npmFailureAdvice only understands 401/403/404/402/429; a process killed by the Windows runtime has no HTTP answer and fell through to the generic branch. Measured: both debug logs of the 0.3.6 attempt stop after the tarball notice with no request, and two identical direct calls exited 0
limits: names only the two codes this machine produced (0xC0000409, 0xC0000005); another Windows exception still prints raw
does not retry the publish: the advice tells the operator to run the direct call
cannot prove the crash was the runtime rather than npm; it proves no HTTP request was logged
no live artifact is possible: this is advice printed by a build script

patches.title: The page strangers read first described a project that had stopped existing
patches.symptom: README.md and README.zh-CN.md still opened as "a resident repair layer that mounts on llm/stream" while the project had become eighteen patches across two resident seams, the CLI and the build side; both also said agent/pre-step was unmounted because nobody had measured a rejection, which R23 had
patches.rootCause: the copy channel guards numbers, not shape: gate_copy checks that every prose digit exists in the fact pack and has no opinion about whether the page still describes the product; three numbers (tests, the CLI half, the total) had drifted too
limits: the root README still has no structural guard: a page could describe behaviour the code does not have (BS-13 own family)
it does not change what npm renders until a release carries the new pages
the seam table is hand-maintained prose; nothing compares it with the registry
no live artifact: these are pages, not a seam

patches.title: A listing that pins git bytes while advertising a registry version installs neither
patches.symptom: docs/market-index.json declared version 0.3.8 and a git commit in one entry; that commit carried nineteen patches while 0.3.8 ships thirteen, so a market trusting it would clone bytes the version does not describe
patches.rootCause: the guard checked the shape of the pin and never its meaning: any hex commit and a packages/plugin path passed, and the index could not name the commit containing it, so every document commit forced a re-pin
limits: it does not turn the repository into a published artifact: the patches it names stay merged and unreleased
a git source needs an explicit unreleased marker; "newest" is a fact read at release time, not checked over the network
it fixes the index this project publishes; a third party that already read this repository is out of reach

patches.title: The published package advertised a subpath that never had a module
patches.symptom: packages/plugin/package.json exported "./retry-listener" -> ./dist/retry-listener.js, but no src/retry-listener.ts has ever existed: the second seam module is failure-listener.ts, already re-exported from the main entry. import "dsh-remedy/retry-listener" fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND while the manifest says it is supported. The dead subpath shipped in 0.3.8 and 0.4.0
patches.rootCause: tests/unit/package-files.test.ts checked the target string against a regex, not the file behind it: ./dist/retry-listener.js matches the pattern exactly as well as ./dist/repair-stream.js does. The exports map was written by hand when the second seam landed, and nothing compared it with src/. This is the same family as P-0010, P-0014, P-0016 and P-0020: the guard reads the form of the promise, not whether it can be kept
limits: it checks the source tree, not the packed tarball: a module that exists in src/ but is excluded by files would still pass
it does not check main or bin against src/, although both are pinned by the same test file
it does not check that an exported subpath is documented, or that a documented subpath is exported
no live artifact is possible: this is a manifest, not a resident seam

patches.title: The drift test repaired the drift before it looked for it
patches.symptom: tests/unit/fixtures-sync.test.ts ran sync_fixtures.mjs in write mode and then compared the copy with the canonical fixtures, so the copy step overwrote any drift before the assertion ran; the read-only --check mode existed but no consumer used it
patches.rootCause: the test was written as setup plus assertion and the setup was the same operation it claimed to verify, so the negative control had nowhere to run
limits: prepack still runs write mode: packing has to create the copy, only the test is read-only first
the negative control corrupts one fixture; a drift that changes the file set is handled by --check but not exercised
the --source/--target/--checksums flags are a test seam and nothing pins them beyond this test file
no live artifact is possible: this is a build-side test

patches.title: The workflow first step was a sentence nobody read
patches.symptom: AGENTS.md says every patch starts with a doc in docs/patches/, but gate_registry resolved only evidence and guards. At the start of R31 the registry held twenty-one patches and docs/patches held nineteen: P-0016 shipped in R24 without a doc while every check stayed green, and INDEX.md still ended its range at P-0015
patches.rootCause: the doc was treated as prose about the patch rather than as part of it. Evidence and guards are paths the registry resolves; a doc was in neither list, so it could be missing with no check noticing. This is the same family as P-0014 and P-0020: a claim about the repository with no reader
limits: it checks that a doc exists, not that it is true: a doc can still describe behaviour the code does not have
it matches by id prefix, which is safe only because registryProblems keeps ids at P-NNNN
an orphan doc with no registry entry is not reported, because the gate iterates the registry rather than the directory
no live artifact is possible: this is a governance gate

patches.title: The two pages npm renders were outside the copy channel
patches.symptom: packages/plugin/README.md and packages/core/README.md were hand-written and absent from docs/copy/manifest.json, so gate_copy never checked their bytes, their fact-pack hash or their writer. P-0017 had narrowed the exposure to "no prose number and every fenced command exists", which is not the same as the channel that every other outward page goes through
patches.rootCause: the copy channel was described as "the outward files at the repository root", and the two package pages were treated as package metadata rather than outward text. A page can be hand-written and still be the first thing a stranger reads; the location of the file was mistaken for the audience
limits: the copy gate checks numbers, bytes and provenance, not truth: a page can still describe behaviour the code does not have
the pages ship inside the tarball, so a change reaches npm only with a release; the manifest is checked in the repository, not against the published tarball
the pages stay hand-written prose that is now registered; a generated page is a different product decision
no live artifact is possible: this is a build-side channel, not a resident seam

patches.title: An unread profile was reported as a finding
patches.symptom: `dsh-remedy explain --sessions <dir>` printed `(no)` in the "enabled here" column for every covered class and exited 1, while its own footer said `enabled-here is unknown: pass --profile-file`; measured: `MALFORMED_RESPONSE 47 P-0001,P-0002,P-0003,P-0005,P-0011 (no)`, exit 1, no profile argument anywhere, and the same command with the desktop profile exited 0
patches.rootCause: `enabled` had two states where the domain has three. `isPatchOn` answered false when the config was null, so "nobody read a profile" became "every coverer is switched off", the cell printed the same `(no)` a measured profile prints, and `uncovered` counted it into the exit code. This project already separates unmeasured from quiet; the command collapsed them
limits: covers "no profile was read"; a profile that is read but declares no switch key still falls back to the command default, which stays unmeasured
exit 0 without a profile means "nothing found", not "nothing wrong": a script wanting the old strictness must pass --profile-file
the table row was tested, not the column widths; a longer patch id still shifts the layout
no live artifact is possible: this is the CLI answering from the registry and an optional file

patches.title: The release procedure had two homes, and the older one was retired
patches.symptom: docs/PUBLISH.md described the procedure this repository uses (scripts/publish_packages.mjs, a token that bypasses the one-time password, commit-tree instead of the missing subtree subcommand), while docs/HANDOFF.md still told a successor to run the pnpm filter publish path and to expect OTP, and its boundary section said the two profiles pointed at a 0.3.5 tarball and that npm latest was 0.3.5
patches.rootCause: handoff-truth.test.ts checks the status table and "第一件事"; the release procedure and the boundary section sit after the evidence index, so they were outside the live contract while still being the sections a successor acts on. A procedure with two homes rots in the one nobody reads, and the stale one was the one the instructions pointed at
limits: the test pins the shape of the sections, not the truth of every step: a PUBLISH.md step can still be wrong while the flags it names are real
it forbids the retired commands by pattern, so a differently worded wrong command is not caught
the boundary section rule looks for .tmp/ paths and a `latest` version; a stale statement phrased without either is still unread
no live artifact is possible: this is documentation and a governance test

patches.title: A fragment dispatched under a name nobody proved
patches.symptom: a fused text gluing two different tools sent the surplus call as the first tool`s name (INVALID_ARGS, measured twice on rc.3)
patches.rootCause: the rescue proves the JSON split and nothing else; the stream names one tool per index and the engine reused it for every fragment
limits: the proof was widened by P-0030 (a required list, a closed schema, or a declared value that breaks its own type/enum): an open schema with no required list still proves nothing, so its fragments keep the stream name and book the residue
the fallback name is not a tool, so the model pays one UNKNOWN_TOOL round trip before it can retry; that is the cost of not running the wrong tool
a fragment that happens to satisfy the wrong tool schema is still dispatched as that tool; schemas are a filter, not a proof
the declarations come from options.tools; a hand-built call or a CLI repair carries none, so nothing changes there

patches.title: A published sample carried this machine's home path
patches.symptom: every tarball since 0.1.0 shipped a fixture whose fused arguments carried the real workspace path (cd "C:/Users/<account>/Desktop/…"), and the public repository carried the same account name in six patch docs, the handoff, a step review and one artifact. Reported by the dshopen maintainer on 2026-11-14 (#472)
patches.rootCause: redaction was wired into the artifact writers (record_*.mjs, scan --out, the journal) and never into the fixture corpus; P-0004 fixed the reader for three path shapes, not the files already tracked. The rule lived where data is produced, not where it leaves the machine
limits: the fixture now carries <home>, so it is no longer a byte-for-byte copy of the session; its note says so and the glued JSON shape is untouched
the rule scans the shipped set and forbids an absolute Users/ segment; a path in another shape (encoded, POSIX home) is caught only by the P-0004 redactor
docs and artifacts were rewritten in place with unchanged stamps: a redaction repair, not a re-measurement
no live artifact: a corpus and channel fix, not a resident seam

patches.title: The pointers a successor acts on were prose nobody compared
patches.symptom: the live handoff called v0.4.2 the newest release after 0.4.3/0.4.4/0.4.5 had gone out, its five-minute check still commented "# 0.4.1", and docs/PUBLISH.md still said npm was at 0.4.2 — the three lines a new session starts from — and every gate stayed green
patches.rootCause: handoff-truth compared the evidence index with files; release-procedure compared the shape of the publish commands; gate_size compared the build with the caps. No rule compared a live version claim with packages/plugin/package.json, and none read the byte row. The same section also told the next agent to pay a patch by splitting modules by load path, which cannot work while the total is the binding cap: the total is the sum of both halves
limits: offline rules: they compare the row with packages/plugin/package.json, not with GitHub or npm, so a row can name the right version and still describe a tag nobody published
the release-body comparison is quoted, not fetched; the v0.4.5 check was manual, not a mechanism
the channel rows in docs/distribution/README.md are dated readings no test reads, so they can go stale between rounds
no runtime behaviour changes; a core release is needed to make the entry visible on npm

patches.title: The name check read required and nothing else, and its counter was a running total
patches.symptom: two gaps after P-0027: a declaration with no required list proved nothing, so a fragment kept the stream name even when its schema rejected it; and one repair's unattributed count landed on every later repair in the same stream ([1,1] instead of [1,0])
patches.rootCause: the check was written against an imagined schema: dsh-tools never sets additionalProperties (dsh-tools/lib/index.js:800-808), so an undeclared key is not proof. The counter bug was a scoping mistake above the per-decision loop
limits: an open schema cannot prove a fragment foreign by its keys, which is the shape of every first-party tool
fits is not identity: a fragment valid for the named tool is still dispatched as that tool
only the dsh-tools dialect was read; another dialect reads unproven more often, which is the safe direction

patches.title: The engine every mount loads had no budget, and a comment said it did
patches.symptom: P-0012 said core sits outside the size gate and a governance test claimed the package has "its own budget"; no cap existed anywhere, and by R41 the engine every mount loads had reached 98 247 emitted bytes
patches.rootCause: the budget predates the 0.4.0 split, which added a second package without a second measurement; "its own budget" described a plan, not a file
limits: the cap covers emitted core JavaScript only: .d.ts, fixtures and package-root files are outside it
it caps the total and the registry file, not each of the other nine modules
core is still not part of residency: the startup account is two rows read together
the cap forces a decision (split the registry, or sign a raise) rather than fixing a defect once

patches.title: The ledger carried the narrative its patch docs already carried
patches.symptom: the eight longest records measured 2 107-2 377 bytes each while the registry had 1 697 bytes left, so the next patch could not be recorded without a raise disguised as a split; the duplication was also loaded on every mount that answers status or explain
patches.rootCause: the registry and docs/patches/ were both written in long form, so symptom, mechanism and limits existed twice while the code reads only id, title, surface, status, severity, evidence, guards, failureClasses and switchKey
limits: the first batch compacts 8 of 31 records; the other 23 keep their long form until they are touched
the 68 000 registry cap did not move: measured 66 303 before and 61 509 after, so this is de-duplication, not a reallocation
no per-record length threshold was added: a threshold needs the owner signature PROJECT_RULES section 1 requires, and this round did not have one
the prose removed from a record is only safe while its doc still says it, and gate_registry checks that a doc exists, not what it says (BS-19)

patches.title: A tool call with no identity was refused and then dispatched anyway
patches.symptom: a block whose id and name were both empty (measured upstream on 0.2.2-rc.3, discussion #13211) was counted as refused and passed through unchanged, so the host persisted tool/call with an empty callId and the V4 session could never resume: "tool/result requires toolCallId matching its tool source"
patches.rootCause: the block-end rejection path was written for fusion refusals, where passing the original through fails the turn visibly; an identity refusal does not fail visibly, it persists a call the host cannot dispatch and a result it cannot match
limits: the adapter that emits an incomplete call is not fixed: this seam names it and keeps the session resumable
a block whose arguments are fused and whose identity is empty is still refused before any split, so it goes out as one call (missing-id fires first)
the verdict stays quiet because no fusion was seen; the rejected event is the only record of the refusal
arguments that parse to a non-object are untouched: that is the other half of #12064

patches.title: A failed stream that no refusal explained was booked as a quiet one
patches.symptom: a turn ended with MALFORMED_RESPONSE and the journal booked nothing: no `errors`, no `refused`, no event (upstream #11337: a reasoning block, then "unsupported stop reason refusal", turn dies)
patches.rootCause: `isFusionFailure` reads the code alone, so every MALFORMED_RESPONSE inherited the fusion path's assumption that a refusal had already booked it
limits: the adapter is not fixed: `stopReason()` still rejects `refusal`, so the turn still ends; this seam names it
the verdict is untouched, so `quiet` still means the fusion defect was not seen
the reproduction is synthetic at the seam; the host half is the shipped `stopReason()` source

patches.title: A patch-layer row promised a module nothing resolved
patches.symptom: every `name:` in `cordis.patch.yml` promises an importable module and neither this repository nor the host checks before load time; #12318 shows the cost: `never started`, every resume fails
patches.rootCause: the namespace gate checked the shape of the rows but never resolved one against the exports it points into, so a rename in `src/` was only caught by a stranger installing the tarball
limits: it proves a row resolves against this manifest, not that the host loads it
a row naming another package is accepted when it is declared, which is not proof of its subpath
it runs in the test suite, not at load time; no live artifact is possible

patches.title: The host erased the id a delta-only stream had proved
patches.symptom: a delta-only tool call assembled as `id: ""` and the session could not resume (upstream #8653)
patches.rootCause: assembler.ts:72 assigns toolCallId unguarded while :73 guards the name, and :115 falls back only from null
limits: the host is not fixed; a different real id on one index passes through, so id-collision-split stays open
not verified: the red is at the seam, no live turn this round produced the shape

patches.title: One dropped closing delimiter killed the turn, and no proof was tried
patches.symptom: a nested argument one `]` short (upstream #12819: "Expected ',' or ']' after array element at position 2963", three times in one session) was refused as `single-object` and re-thrown, so the whole turn died
patches.rootCause: the single-object branch had two outcomes, a proven reseal or a refusal, and a text one delimiter from parsing was neither; the splitter never saw it (`unbalanced: input ends at depth 1`)
limits: pi-ai route only: dsh-llm-deepseek reports "tool input is invalid JSON" without the text, so nothing reaches this seam
a missing final delimiter and an ambiguous text are refused, never guessed
verified on Linux (WSL2) against a scripted provider, not on a real model turn: the repair and the dispatch are live, the shape is synthesized

patches.title: The redaction was written on one platform and shipped to three
patches.symptom: a macOS or Linux home path went through `redact()` untouched (`/Users/alice/x.ts`, `file:///Users/alice/x.ts`, `--Users-alice-x--`, `--home-alice-x--`), so the account name would have left the machine in an artifact; 5 of 8 measured shapes leaked
patches.rootCause: two rules each assumed a Windows drive letter: `windows-home` starts with [A-Za-z]:, and `encoded-home` required `X-Users-`. The session key is built by `projectKey` (app.asar, dsh-session-persistence-jsonl/src/format.ts) which turns every / \ : into one `-` and wraps the slug in `--…--`, so the same project encodes as --C-Users-…, --Users-… or --home-… and only the first one matched
limits: the three shapes are tested as strings, not produced on their own platform, so this is not "tested on macOS"
/root/ is deliberately not redacted: the account name is the same string for everyone
the plugin itself stays platform-independent; only the evidence layer had a platform assumption
build scripts keep their WINDOWS branch on purpose (Node cannot spawn npm.cmd without a shell)

patches.title: A recorder that only worked on Windows, and said "no sessions" when it failed
patches.symptom: three recorders computed `.dsh/sessions` on Linux/macOS (`USERPROFILE` is unset there) and exited 3 with "no session directory"; an empty `DSH_SESSIONS=` was accepted as the root, pointing them at the current directory
patches.rootCause: `process.env.USERPROFILE ?? join(...)` turned "the variable is missing" into "the home is the empty string", and a join of an empty home is a relative path. `HOMEDIR()`-based `record_live_mount.mjs` was the one that worked on both platforms
limits: not "runs on macOS": the POSIX branch it takes is the Linux one measured here
an empty HOME still cannot be resolved; the fallback is a literal ~/.dsh/sessions, not a lookup
the plugin never read USERPROFILE; only these offline recorders did

patches.title: The acceptance recorder owned a fixture count the package owns
patches.symptom: a green published package was recorded as a failed install: the cold directory installed, verify printed eight PASS lines and OK 8 fixture(s), and the recorder still answered "verify did not print OK 6 fixture(s)" because it looked for a literal six
patches.rootCause: R49 added two canonical fixtures, so the count became eight in three places and stayed six in a fourth: record_install_acceptance.mjs carried both a regex and a claimed string with the old number. Same family as P-0008 / P-0029: a number nobody compared with the thing it describes
limits: the criterion is the count plus every PASS line, not fixture contents: verify still owns what each case must decide
it cannot name which fixture drifted; sync_fixtures --check owns that
an npm exec that exits 0 with no output stays a failure here

patches.title: The installed CLI was silent on Linux, and exited 0
patches.symptom: the installed bin printed nothing and exited 0 on Linux (and by the same code path on macOS), while node dist/cli.js verify printed the full result: the one command every acceptance and README quotes verified nothing and reported success
patches.rootCause: the entry guard compared import.meta.url (the resolved file) with pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]) (what the caller named), and npm installs a POSIX bin as a symlink, so the two differ and main() never ran. Windows installs a .cmd shim passing the real path, which is why 0.1.0-0.4.11 never saw it
limits: 0.4.11 carries the old guard: the fix ships in 0.4.12, and 0.4.11 stays installable but silent through its bin
the fix makes the command run; it adds no output of its own
